assets.prompt:
Subject: Explain the agent–environment interaction loop from the Neural Atlas article "Agentic Environment Engineering for Large Language Models": an agent selects an action from its interaction history, the environment transitions its state, and observations and reward return to the agent.

Intent: Generate one publication-ready, source-locked technical diagram for an AI engineering article. Show ONLY this mechanism, with minimum necessary elements and maximum semantic precision. This is a single coherent mechanism, not the entire environment-engineering ecosystem.

Source facts supplied from the article: the policy is π(a_t | h_t), the state transition is P(s_(t+1) | s_t,a_t), observations come from O, rewards from R. The agent acts from history of observations, actions, and rewards; the underlying environment state is distinct from what the agent observes. Do not invent any other facts. Do not display equations or timestep numbers; the words below express these facts.

Required visible content, exact labels:
- A left outlined container titled "Agent". Inside it, a small box "Interaction history" above a small box "Policy". A short downward connector from history to policy; no label needed.
- A right outlined container titled "Environment". Inside it, one small box "State transition".
- One upper orthogonal arrow from Policy's right edge into State transition's left edge, routed through the open central gap, labeled "Action".
- One lower return path from State transition's bottom edge, routed beneath both containers and entering Interaction history's left edge. Its arrowhead must terminate precisely at Interaction history. Label it "Observation + reward".
No additional components, icons, symbols, metrics, values, side notes, legend, title or subtitle. The containment and connection labels are sufficient context.

Hierarchy and layout: clean landscape composition, generous white space, left Agent and right Environment horizontally aligned. Main container headings slightly larger than the internal labels. The feedback loop must be completely legible and traceable: Policy -> State transition -> Interaction history -> Policy. No crossed connectors, no detached arrowheads, no arrows ending in empty space. Keep the bottom feedback route outside the containers except where it enters its destination. Real connections take priority over symmetry.

Background: pure white, completely blank. No grid, no texture, no shadows, no gradient.
Style: flat vector-like research-paper schematic; dark charcoal readable sans-serif typography; thin uniform charcoal outlines; small-radius corners; action and feedback connectors in restrained blue. Every line conveys containment or directional flow. No decorative glyphs, neural network motifs, artificial node arrays, badges, or section numbers. This prompt has a written style specification but no visual reference image, so do not pretend to match an unseen reference.

Quality: crisp edges, precise alignment, readable short labels, consistent type scale and line weight, ample padding, no truncation or warped letters. Do not add content to fill empty space. No fake measurements, timestamps, IDs, worker counts, examples, service names, unsupported architecture layers, marketing copy, logos, watermarks, dark backgrounds, photorealism or 3D effects. Render only the specified mechanism.
